title: Scan watchdog in the cmd_vel safety filter

notes.what: When no LaserScan has arrived for longer than scan_timeout, the filter publishes a zero Twist instead of forwarding the command, with a throttled warning. The hard-coded stop distance becomes the stop_distance parameter.
notes.why: A dead lidar used to look like an empty world: the last scan showed no obstacle so commands kept flowing. The check lives in the cmd_vel callback because the scan callback stops running the moment scans stop.
notes.edge: Scan age is header.stamp against the node clock, so a lidar whose clock runs behind makes every scan look stale and the robot refuses to move. stop_distance set to 0 silently disables the obstacle stop since min_range can never be below it.
notes.risk: Launch files that relied on the constant must now pass stop_distance; the default keeps the old value. The watchdog adds a clock read per command, negligible. Throttled logging hides repeated stops in bag replays.
notes.test: Publish synthetic LaserScan messages from a test node, stop publishing, send a cmd_vel_raw and assert /cmd_vel is a zero Twist; launch_testing with a sim clock keeps it repeatable.
